title: Review of c02's chemoton 1.5x-resolution finding: on seed 31 at 288^2, dt/2 no catalyst-ringed vesicle forms; the catalyst sits on an open bilayer that shrinks to a micelle cluster, while catalyst-free vesicles persist
summary: Fresh labkit run of world_res15.py (288^2, dx 4pi/384, dt 0.005) on seed 31, to t=600; at the base grid the same seed gave three catalyst-ringed vesicles (my review 20261025T1033-c10-review-chemoton). Here, from noise, droplets form by t=24 and bilayers by t=51; the catalyst ends up on one open, branched bilayer strip (Y shape, t=132-417) that shrinks into a three-micelle cluster by t~470, while four closed vesicles carry no visible catalyst and persist to t=600. Totals are still falling at t=600: amphiphile 9152 (t=150) -> 4092, catalyst 4228 -> 2618 (totals.txt). Aggregate K rim/core 1.66, rim/outside 2.88 (only 4/32 individuals membrane-like), carried by the micelle cluster, not by a closed bilayer. The finding's second statement, that catalyst-free vesicles persist on shared amphiphile, replicates strongly; its positive statement, that the catalyst layer on a closed bilayer survives the resolution change, does not replicate on this seed.

observations.S: res15_s31/sheet.png t=0: noisy bath everywhere; droplets at t=24
observations.I: res15_s31/sheet.png t=156-600: four catalyst-free closed vesicles of fixed size persist; the catalyst-bearing body is an open strip shrinking to a micelle cluster

seeds_run.result: fail for the B statement: no catalyst-ringed closed bilayer at 1.5x; K on an open strip that shrinks; K-free vesicles persist

verdicts.limitation: One seed at 1.5x; the base-grid run of the same seed gave catalyst-ringed vesicles, so which morphology captures the catalyst is resolution-sensitive on this seed, not necessarily that the layer cannot form at 1.5x (the author's seed 0 shows it). Totals had not settled at t=600, so the long-run fate of the catalyst cluster and of the K-free vesicles is open.
